recommendations: Fix lines 180 and 193 in STRspy_run_v2.0_Args.sh to check `[[ -f "src/STRspy_Normal_v2.0_Args.sh" ]]` (and `src/STRspy_Parallel_v2.0_Args.sh`) matching the `bash src/...` invocation below them.

Update README.md line 120 to include the required getopts flags (`bash ./STRspy_run_v2.0_Args.sh -i config/InputConfig.txt -t config/UserToolsConfig.txt -j normal`) and align `THREAD` vs `THREADS` in config/InputConfig.txt.
Pin `python>=3.9` and `samtools>=1.12` in `setup/STRspy_2.0_env.yml` so clean Linux environments do not pull a legacy OpenSSL 1.0 samtools binary.
Tag a GitHub release for STRspy v2.0 on the default branch so users and automated evaluators resolve v2.0 by default instead of v1.1.1 (2021).

verdict.title: Fails in manual verification
verdict.reason: Even after creating the Conda environment, generating config/UserToolsConfig.txt, and supplying the -i and -t flags omitted by README line 120, the unmodified upstream wrapper STRspy_run_v2.0_Args.sh fails immediately with exit code 1: lines 180 and 193 check `if [[ -f "STRspy_Normal_v2.0_Args.sh" ]]` in the repository root even though the script lives under `src/STRspy_Normal_v2.0_Args.sh` (which line 199 then invokes). Because the file check and invocation path disagree, the wrapper exits with `please make sure you are in the same directory of STRspy` from any working directory.

conclusion.title: Repeatability of this manual run
conclusion.body: The pinned upstream commit, prepared environment description, exact commands executed, and sanitized terminal output recorded in this report document the procedure for independent reproduction.

limitations: Results apply exclusively to the exact Git commit SHA and manually prepared environment recorded in this report.
Single regional reference slice per input type; low-coverage warnings on sliced BAMs do not imply defects on whole-genome data.
Plausible Output checks verify structural format and recognizable STR loci, not biological genotype truth.
Verification is a point-in-time snapshot; upstream repository changes after this commit are not covered until re-verification.
No truth-set concordance, forensic casework validation, or regulatory compliance assessment was performed.
